| 3 | **Pass C** | **ρ** in assignment |

---

## Headline

Alex is pleased. You’re not off track. The Pass work is **right**. The shift is **directedness**: fewer items, clearer hierarchy, outputs as a **characterization slide series** — and a hard line between **sensitivity analysis** (now) and **statistical parameter fitting** (next big insight).

His closing: *“This is still basically what I asked for two weeks ago… we need to be more directed.”*

---

## What landed well

**Pass C / ρ:** Assortativity answered cleanly — flat without ρ, roster/peer effect appears with ρ. He called that “really good.”

**Pass B / λ:** Directionally right (λ = 0 vs λ > 0 bends the curve), but **incomplete** — needs the same systematic treatment as ρ, plus the double-plot ask below.

**Pass A / empirical:** The real-data side-by-side (talent vs poolq_loo) is the anchor. The “two x-axes” conversation is about making the **generative** slides show the same dual readout the empirical slide already implies.

**Model simplicity:** Collapsed **L_C** is fine for this paper. B vs D decomposition is parked — development benefits of good teams are real but not identifiable in promotion data yet → one black-box **L**.

**Sweep infrastructure:** Rivanna/sweep code is good; reshape output into a **standard slide series** (equations at top, bold the knob, figures below) — not one-off PNGs.

---

## Three layers (don’t merge them)

### Layer 1 — Gallery fixes (build on what you have)

Concrete asks from looking at the deck:

1. **λ ablation panel** — mirror Pass C’s ρ panel: fix ρ, vary λ (e.g. four subplots at your four ρ values, or a fixed-ρ sweep).
2. **Double-plot in simulation** — one run (e.g. λ = 0.55, ρ fixed):
   - **Left:** 16 bins on **individual A_i** (sort 1→n, then bin)
   - **Right:** 16 bins on **poolq_loo** (team average talent, LOO)
   - Same scenario both sides — not separate model runs with different λ.
3. **Overlay λ = 0 vs λ > 0** on the **A_i-binned** side for deltas.
4. **Put sort-and-chop back** on the Pass C ρ figure (you cut it because it squished the panel).
5. **Report fitted inputs:** distribution of **t_j**, **σ²**, etc. — notation that **data-fitted** quantities (t̃, empirical draws) differ from **simulation-drawn** ones.

Alex called these “puzzle pieces” — important, but not the deepest insight.

### Layer 2 — Main mission now: sensitivity characterization (~4 days)

> Vary **one knob at a time**; keep everything else fixed; show how the **two curves** move.

**The two curves** (throughout the meeting):

- binned by **A_i** → monotone talent ladder  
- binned by **poolq_loo / L_C** → inverted-U / roster-pressure shape  

**Knobs to characterize** (one slide each: 3 core equations, **bold the knob**, figure below):

| Knob | Alex’s expectation |
|------|-------------------|
| **ρ** | Matters a lot (Pass C shows this) |
| **λ** | Matters a lot (Pass B starts it; needs full panel) |
| **θ** (sigmoid center) | Matters; likely tied to **K/N** (success rate), not “median of selected” |
| **γ** (sigmoid slope) | Characterize |
| **Distribution of A_i** | Probably doesn’t matter much (CLT on team averages) — but **document** choice + SI robustness |
| **Distribution of t_j** | Fix from empirical ballpark; characterize |
| **K/N** (selection rate) | **System feature** — “everybody gets a trophy” vs highly selective regimes |

**Not yet:** full statistical fitting to real data. At ~41:44: *“I’m not caring about fitting to data yet — just characterize what’s going on.”*

**Pace:** ~two knobs per day → ~four days for a solid characterization deck. **Checkpoint with Alex after the first two** (ρ and λ).

### Layer 3 — Next big insight (after characterization): statistical fitting, not curve matching

**Do NOT:** pick ρ or λ by minimizing distance between empirical Hero curve and simulated curve → that’s **curve fitting**.

**DO:** define a **statistic of the raw data** for each parameter:

- **ρ:** e.g. **within-team correlation of ability** (maybe log-transformed) — model-invariant, computable from data alone  
- **λ:** a **roster-pressure statistic** — autocorrelation / “if a teammate gets promoted, what does that tell you about your odds?” — **not** the sim selection-score formula  

If you nail that, you’re “putting a metric on the effect” and “really going somewhere.”

PD14 magnitude (Model A vs B predictive comparison) is **related** but PD15 is sharper: estimators tied to **parameters**, not just better prediction. **Park magnitude until characterization is done** unless Alex says otherwise.

---

## Other model notes from the conversation

- **B/D vs L:** Use **L_C** only for now; future work could split λ_B and λ_D.
- **Notation:** σ used twice (team σ_j vs sigmoid σ) — fix. **θ** = sigmoid center (not median of selected). **γ** = sigmoid slope.
- **θ and K/N:** Centering θ likely depends on **K/N** (draft slots / population), a fixed **system property** (MBB vs Army differ) — sweep it, don’t collapse it.
- **A_i distribution:** Alex expects **robustness** (enough spread; CLT on team means), not power-law dependence — show alternatives in SI.
- **Process:** 57-item checklist is too many; same failure mode as cranking calculations that feel like progress but aren’t the mission.

---

## How this supersedes the old checklist

`CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md` was re-entry + run Pass A/B + PD14 magnitude. That scaffold did its job.

PD15 says **archive it** and replace with something shorter, phased:

**Phase A — Gallery honesty (1–2 days)**  
λ panel, sim double-plots, sort-and-chop back, fitted-distribution callouts.

**Phase B — Characterization deck (~4 days)**  
ρ → λ → θ/γ → A distribution → t_j → K/N. Checkpoint after ρ + λ.

**Phase C — Statistical fitting (later)**  
Data statistics for ρ̂ and λ̂; then revisit PD14 magnitude.

**Still parked:** B/D split, Rivanna hero rebuild, army figures, bin-16 prose polish.

1. **Board vs screen:** When Alex said “flat without assortativity,” was that **Pass C on screen**? (I’m assuming yes.)  
2. **Double-plot target:** Left = A_i-binned, right = poolq_loo-binned, same sim run — still your read?  
3. **λ sign on Model slide:** You corrected him (λ = 0.55, L_C negative) — what’s on **Model.pptx** now?  
4. **PD14:** Park until after Phase B, or keep as parallel track?

---

## Bottom line

You didn’t waste the last two weeks. Alex said the Pass work is **right**. The job now is **directed characterization** — fewer checklist items, standard slides, two curves every time — then **fit ρ and λ to data statistics**, not to curve shape.

When you want, we can archive `CHARLES_CHECKLIST.md` and draft a **~15–20 item PD15 checklist** using **Pass A / B / C as on your slides**.

_**User**_

Please give me a definition for what you think Alex means when he says he wants us to "characterize" the variables

---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Here’s how I read Alex’s use of **“characterize”** in PD15 — in one sentence and then in operational terms.

## One sentence

**Characterize** = for each model knob, run a disciplined **sensitivity study** in the simulator: hold everything else fixed, sweep that knob, and show **how the two outcome curves move** — so you can say *what matters, what barely matters, and what the knob actually does* in your framework.

It is **not** (yet) “pick the knob value that makes the sim look like the empirical Hero plot.”

---

## What it is

Alex wants a **standardized slide series** where each slide answers:

> “If I change **only this** parameter, what happens to the model’s behavior?”

For each variable (ρ, λ, θ, γ, distribution of A_i, distribution of t_j, K/N):

1. **Write the three core equations** at the top of the slide.
2. **Bold the one knob** you’re perturbing.
3. **Fix all other settings** to your baseline (539 preset, etc.).
4. **Sweep that knob** across a sensible range (or show a few representative values).
5. **Plot the two curves** Alex keeps returning to:
   - **Curve 1:** draft/selection rate binned by **individual A_i** (sort 1→n, 16 bins)
   - **Curve 2:** same sim run, binned by **poolq_loo / L_C** (16 bins)
6. **Interpret:** Does the inverted-U appear/disappear? Does the monotone ladder change? Does anything happen at all?

That’s characterization: **mapping knob → qualitative (and optionally quantitative) changes in the model’s readouts.**

---

## What it is not

Alex was explicit about boundaries:

| Not characterization | Why |
|----------------------|-----|
| **Curve fitting** — tune ρ or λ until sim matches empirical Hero | That’s minimizing curve distance, not understanding the model |
| **Statistical fitting to data** (for now) | Layer 3 comes *after* characterization (~41:44: “not caring about fitting to data yet”) |
| **One-off gallery PNGs** without the slide template | Output should be a **repeatable series**, not ad hoc figures |
| **Changing multiple knobs at once** | One-at-a-time unless you’re explicitly doing a designed interaction later |

---

## What “done” looks like for each knob

For each parameter, you should be able to say something like:

- **ρ:** “Matters a lot — without it, peer/roster effect is flat; with it, inverted-U emerges.” (Pass C already shows this.)
- **λ:** “Matters a lot — need the same systematic panel as ρ.” (Pass B is a start, not finished.)
- **θ / γ:** “Sigmoid center/slope change selection sharpness; θ likely scales with **K/N** (success rate).”
- **Distribution of A_i:** “Probably **robust** if there’s enough spread (CLT on team averages) — document one default + SI alternatives.”
- **Distribution of t_j:** “Fix a reasonable default from data ballpark; show sensitivity.”
- **K/N:** “System feature, not collapsible — in ‘everybody gets a trophy’ regimes, roster pressure shouldn’t matter much; in highly selective regimes, it should bite harder.”

Characterization is **complete** when you have that kind of statement **backed by plots** for each knob, not when every parameter matches real data.

---

## How it differs from “fit” (Alex’s later step)

| **Characterize** (now) | **Fit** (later) |
|------------------------|-----------------|
| Inside the **simulator** | On **real data** |
| “What does this knob *do*?” | “What value does the data imply?” |
| One knob at a time, fixed baseline | Estimator tied to a **defined statistic** (e.g. within-team correlation for ρ) |
| Qualitative + sensitivity plots | Numeric λ̂, ρ̂ with statistical meaning |

Characterization tells you **which knobs are worth fitting** and **what to expect** when you fit them. Fitting tells you **what the basketball (or Army) system’s numbers are.**

---

## Practical test (Charles-facing)

You’ve characterized a variable when you can put it on one slide and tell Alex:

1. **What we held fixed**
2. **What we varied**
3. **What happened to both curves**
4. **Whether it matters for the story** (essential / nice-to-have / probably robust / system-dependent)

If you can only say “I ran a sweep on Rivanna,” you’ve **computed** — but not **characterized** in Alex’s sense until it’s shaped into that slide + interpretation.

---

**Bottom line:** Alex’s “characterize” is **model sensitivity analysis with a fixed reporting template** — understand the machine before you calibrate it to data. That’s why he budgeted ~4 days and ~2 knobs per day, and why he said to checkpoint after ρ and λ.

OK buddy, as an aside I thought of something that is a little puzzling to me.  It seems plausible to me that we could set all variables at some baseline and then just modifying them one at a time might never give us the hero style curve, perhaps 2 or 3 of them would need to be varied simultaneously to create such a curve and any one variable's dynamic range might not do it.  Did I explain myself well?

---

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Yes — you explained it well. That’s a real limitation of **one-at-a-time (OAT)** sweeps, and it’s worth keeping in mind.

## What you’re saying

At a fixed baseline, you vary **only ρ**, or **only λ**, or **only θ**, etc. It’s plausible that:

- No single knob, over its full allowed range, reproduces the Hero-style inverted-U.
- The curve might need **joint settings** — e.g. λ > 0 **and** ρ high enough **and** selective enough K/N.
- So OAT could make a knob look ** irrelevant** when it’s actually **necessary but not sufficient**.

That’s the classic **interaction / epistasis** problem: OAT tells you each knob’s **marginal** effect *holding everything else fixed*, not what happens when knobs **work together**.

## Why Alex still wants OAT first

In PD15, “characterize” doesn’t mean “prove the Hero exists from scratch by finding the one magic knob.” It means:

> At our **working baseline** (539 preset, etc.), what does each knob **do** to the two readout curves?

You **already** have evidence the combo can produce hero-like behavior:

- **Pass A:** real data shows the shape.
- **Pass B:** λ in score bends the curve (at fixed ρ and other settings).
- **Pass C:** ρ brings out the peer effect (at fixed λ in score).

So OAT is less “discover the inverted-U” and more “**map the machine** around a point we know works.”

## Where your worry bites hardest

Your concern is strongest for knobs that are **conditionally active**:

| Knob | Might look flat in OAT when… |
|------|------------------------------|
| **ρ** | λ = 0 (no roster pressure in score) — you and Alex touched this in the transcript |
| **λ** | ρ ≈ 0 (no assortative sorting → weak L_C variation) |
| **θ, γ** | K/N very high (“everybody gets a trophy”) |
| **K/N** | Other knobs at values where selection barely binds |

At a **bad baseline**, OAT sweeps can look boring — and that’s actually informative: *“At this baseline, knob X alone doesn’t move the curves.”*

At the **539 baseline**, Alex expects ρ and λ to **matter a lot** — Pass B/C are already partial proof.

## What Alex is not asking for (yet)

He’s **not** asking you to grid-search ρ × λ × θ until you match the empirical Hero bin-for-bin. That would blur into **curve fitting**, which he rejected.

He **is** asking for disciplined marginal maps first, then checkpoint with him after ρ and λ.

## Practical takeaway for you

1. **OAT is the first pass**, not the last word — especially for ρ and λ, which likely **interact**.
2. **Baseline matters** — characterize around the **working** preset, not arbitrary defaults.
3. **After ρ + λ OAT**, a natural **Phase B+** question (maybe at Alex checkpoint) is:  
   *“Do we need a small 2D panel (e.g. ρ × λ) to show the hero regime, even if one-at-a-time alone doesn’t?”*  
   That’s consistent with science and doesn’t replace OAT — it **complements** it.
4. **Pass A stays the anchor** — the stylized fact in data; sim characterization explains **mechanism**, not re-discovery of the curve from zero.

## One-sentence version

You’re right that **one knob alone might never generate the Hero curve**; Alex’s OAT plan assumes a **working baseline** and aims to **label each knob’s role**, with **interactions** (especially ρ × λ) as the obvious next layer if marginal sweeps look too flat.

If you want, we can add a short **“OAT caveat / interaction note”** to `PD15_notes.docx` so future-you doesn’t forget this when building the characterization deck.

Good catch. **`\,` is LaTeX thin-space**, not multiplication — and our slide renderer (`gallery_mathtext`) doesn't interpret it, so it was showing up as literal `\ ,` in PowerPoint.

### What I fixed

1. **Slide formulas** now use **`\cdot`** (renders as **·**):
   - `$S_i = A_i - \lambda \cdot L_C$`
   - `$S_i = A_i - 0.55 \cdot L_C$`
   - Simplified the ρ assign formula (dropped `\frac`, `\left`, etc. that also weren't rendering)

2. **`gallery_mathtext.py`** — any stray `\,` now maps to **·** as a safety net

3. **Regenerated both decks:**
   - `CHAR_rho_characterization.pptx`
   - `CHAR_lambda_characterization.pptx`

Reopen those in PowerPoint — you should see **·** between coefficient and `L_C`, not `\ ,`.

**Note:** Matplotlib PNG captions still use `\,` (matplotlib renders that correctly). Only the PowerPoint text path needed the fix. If you want dots there too for consistency, say the word.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Good find — this was a real bug, not a formatting preference.

**Root cause:** python-pptx 1.0.2 accepts `run.font.subscript = True` but **never writes it to the slide XML**, so PowerPoint showed plain `Ai`, `Si`, `Yselected`.

**Fix:** `gallery_mathtext.py` now sets the Office Open XML **`baseline="-25000"`** attribute directly on subscript runs (and `30000` for superscripts), with slightly smaller font for subscripts.

Verified in XML:
- `S` + subscript `i`
- `L` + subscript `C`  
- `Y` + subscript `selected`

**Regenerated:**
- `CHAR_rho_characterization.pptx`
- `CHAR_lambda_characterization.pptx`

Reopen those in PowerPoint — you should see proper subscripts on `$S_i$`, `$A_i$`, `$L_C$`, `$Y_{\mathrm{selected}}$`, `$T_j$`, `$π_{ij}$`, etc.

This fix applies to all slide builders using `gallery_mathtext` (including Pass A/B/C gallery if you rebuild those).

Your instinct is worth taking seriously. I traced the code and re-ran the sort-and-chop arm — **the assignment step looks correct**; the weird red curve comes from how that roster pairs with **score + top-K**, not from a chop bug.

## What sort-and-chop is supposed to do

From `assign_sort_chop_benchmark` in `tier1_pool_assignment.py`:

```667:696:sports/tier1_pool_assignment.py
def assign_sort_chop_benchmark(
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    ability: np.ndarray,
    n_teams: int,
    *,
    sorting_noise_sd: float = 0.0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """537-style hard assortative assignment: sort by ability, equal-count slices.
    ...
    Sort everyone by ability (optionally + noise), then chop into n_teams contiguous
    blocks of equal size. Talent windows barely overlap (coverage ≈ 1).
    Important: this is NOT "ρ → ∞". Soft ρ and sort-chop are different mechanisms.
    """
    ...
    order = np.argsort(signal, kind="mergesort")
    base = np.repeat(np.arange(n_teams), int(np.ceil(n / n_teams)))[:n]
    pool_id = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    pool_id[order] = base
    return pool_id
```

In plain language:

1. Rank all **15,000** players by **A_i** (seed 42, Beta(2,2) on [0,1]).
2. Cut the sorted list into **1,000** equal slices of **15** → one team per slice.
3. Team 0 = lowest talent block; team 999 = highest.
4. Windows **almost don’t overlap** (median within-team SD ≈ **0.0002** — essentially zero).

That matches the old **537** benchmark: “line them up 1→N and chop,” **not** “turn ρ up to infinity.”

---

## Why the red curve looks crazy on Pass C

Pass C holds **score fixed**: \(S_i = A_i - 0.55\,L_C\), then **global top-1,500** by \(S_i\). Only **assignment** changes across arms.

Under sort-and-chop, each team is a tight talent clump, so:

- **Pool mean ≈ each player’s own ability** (everyone on the team is at the same level).
- On **high-ability teams**, almost every teammate counts as a “viable peer” → **\(L_C\) is very high** (~0.87–0.94 on top teams).
- Score becomes: high \(A_i\) **minus** a big congestion penalty.

I re-ran the sort-chop arm (539, seed 42). Selected players:

| Quantity | Selected players | All players |
|----------|------------------|-------------|
| Ability (median) | **0.604** | max 0.999 |
| Pool mean (median) | **0.604** | 0.012 – 0.990 |
| \(L_C\) (median) | **0.238** | top teams ~0.87 |

So global winners cluster in a **middle band** (~pool mean 0.57–0.64), not at the top. Top teams (998, 999) still get *some* selections (13/15 on team 999), but most of their players lose to mid-tier teams with lower \(L_C\).

That produces the needle you see:

- **Bin 11** (pool-mean quantile ~0.58–0.63): **100%** of players in that bin selected → spike to 1.0.
- **Bins 14–15** (highest pool mean): **~0%** selected.

That’s the “flat … then bump” pattern you described to Alex in PD15 — not a rendering bug.

---

## Algorithm OK; interpretation is the issue

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Is chop implemented wrong? | **No** — disjoint equal slices, as designed. |
| Is it “max ρ”? | **No** — different mechanism from soft ρ (doc 04 says this explicitly). |
| Why spike on a **ρ** figure? | Sort-and-chop + **λ=0.55 congestion** creates a **score optimum in the middle** of the ability ladder; quantile bins turn that into one sharp peak. |
| Same score as ρ arms? | Yes — and that’s exactly why the line behaves so differently. |

Soft ρ arms change **how rosters mix**. Sort-and-chop changes rosters to **hard tiers**, which interacts badly with **\(L_C\)** when every teammate is a viable peer at the top.

---

## Practical takeaway

- **For the ρ story:** the **no-sort-chop** slide is the honest comparison; sort-and-chop isn’t on the same interpretive footing as ρ = 0.1 → 32.
- **If you keep sort-and-chop:** label it **“537 disjoint-slice benchmark (not ρ→∞)”** and add a footnote: *with congestion in score, top-tier clumps get high \(L_C\); global top-K peaks in mid tiers.*
- **To sanity-check visually:** overlay sort-and-chop with **λ = 0** (talent-only score) — you should get a much more monotone, top-heavy curve; the weird shape is mostly **assign × \(L_C\) × top-K**, not chop alone.

I can run that λ=0 overlay next, or add a one-line caveat to the sort-and-chop slide — whichever you prefer.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

There isn’t a “per year” loop in this generative algorithm — it’s **one static league, one selection event per run**.

### Total selected (each run)

| Knob | 539 preset (your Pass C / diagnostic) |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| **`N_SELECTED` (K)** | **1,500** |
| **`N_INDIVIDUALS` (N)** | **15,000** (1,000 teams × 15 roster spots) |
| **Selectivity K/N** | **10%** |

Defined in `sports/tier1_sim_config.py` as `N_SELECTED = 1500`; the sort-and-chop diagnostic uses that via the 539 playground state.

### How selection works

1. **Assign** — sort-and-chop (or soft ρ) builds rosters once  
2. **Score** — compute \(S_i\) for all 15,000 players  
3. **Select** — **`winner_selection = "C"`** = **deterministic top-K**: exactly **1,500** players get `Y_selected = 1`, the rest 0  

No seasons, no re-draw across years — one cross-section meant to echo “one draft cohort” qualitatively.

### If you meant real MBB

The **empirical** Pass A panel is ~2011–2021, but that’s a different pipeline (`530` / panel build). The generative sim doesn’t iterate 11 years; it’s **1,500 winners per simulation run**.

(A separate 539 “full” preset uses `MATCH_539_FULL_N_SELECTED = 3000` on a larger league — not what the current diagnostic uses.)

from sports_pipeline.panel_build import assign_poolq_bin_labels
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('tier1_sim_config', SPORTS/'tier1_sim_config.py')
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
state = {'ability_draw':'beta_2_2','target_dist':'uniform','t_low':0,'t_high':1,'viability_theta':0.72,'viability_sharpness':10,'n_selected':1500,'winner_selection':'C'}
params = tge.assignment_params_from_state(SPORTS, state, tpa=tpa)
rng = np.random.default_rng(HERO_SEED)
ability = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, params.n_individuals, ability_draw=params.ability_draw, ability_mean=params.ability_mean, ability_sd=params.ability_sd, ability_clip_low=params.ability_clip_low, ability_clip_high=params.ability_clip_high, ability_student_t_df=params.ability_student_t_df, ability_student_t_scale=params.ability_student_t_scale)
team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, params.n_teams, target_mean_dist=params.target_mean_dist, target_mean_low=params.target_mean_low, target_mean_high=params.target_mean_high, target_mean_mu=params.target_mean_mu, target_mean_sigma=params.target_mean_sigma)
players_base, _, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method='sort_chop', ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
sel = replace(tge.SelectionConfig.from_module(mod), n_bins=HERO_BINS, bin_mode='quantile', n_selected=1500, winner_selection='C')

def rates(lam):
    sm, pl, w = ('ability','quality',0) if lam<=0 else ('loo_gap_plus_ability','crowding_smooth',lam)
    p = tpa.assign_selection(players_base.copy(), np.random.default_rng(HERO_SEED+int(lam*10000)), n_selected=1500, score_mode=sm, loo_gap_weight=w, winner_selection='C', pool_l_mode=pl, viability_theta=0.72, viability_sharpness=10)
    s = tge.inverted_u_bin_table_team_mean(p, sel, assign_poolq_bin_labels=assign_poolq_bin_labels)
    r = s.set_index('bin')['selection_rate'].sort_index()
    return r

r0 = rates(0)
for lam in np.round(np.arange(0.405, 0.425, 0.005), 3):
    r = rates(lam)
    md = (r-r0).abs().max()
    peak = int(r.idxmax())+1
    print(f'λ={lam:.3f} max|Δvs0|={md:.4f} peak={peak} top={r.iloc[-1]:.3f}')

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Great question — I re-ran a finer λ sweep on the same sort-and-chop rosters (seed 42, 539 preset) to pin this down.

## Why λ=0 and λ=0.25 look identical

On sort-and-chop rosters, **ability and congestion move in lockstep**:

- Teams are equal slices of the talent distribution, so pool mean ≈ team tier.
- **Spearman(Aᵢ, L_C) = 1.0** on these rosters — highest-ability teams also have the highest crowding.
- Score is Sᵢ = Aᵢ − λ·L_C. For small λ, that penalty is too weak to reorder anyone who matters for the **bin-level** curve.

So through λ=0.25 (and actually much higher), the **16-bin selection rates are numerically identical** to λ=0 — max |Δrate| = 0 across all bins. A few individual players swap at the cut line (8 at λ=0.25, more as λ rises), but those swaps stay within bins that already sit at 100% or 0%, so the plotted curve doesn't move.

That's why the green (0.25) line sits under the dashed blue (0) line in the figure — they're the same curve.

## Where monotone → hump

The transition is **sharp**, not gradual:

| λ range | Shape | Peak bin | Top bin rate |
|---------|-------|----------|--------------|
| 0 – **0.415** | Same as talent-only; strictly increasing | 16 | 1.0 |
| **~0.42** | First bin-rate movement; still peak at 16 | 16 | 1.0 |
| **0.44–0.46** | Hump forming; peak shifts left | 12–16 | drops fast |
| **0.50+** | Needle hump | 11 | ~0.27 → 0.02 |

**Practical answer:** the monotone curve holds until roughly **λ ≈ 0.40–0.42** on this seed. The visible hump (peak leaving bin 16) kicks in around **λ ≈ 0.44–0.46**, and by **λ = 0.55** you're at the needle you already plotted (peak bin 11, top bin ~2%).

## Intuition

While λ is small, global top-1500 ≈ top-1500 by talent — congestion can't yet overcome the ability gradient. Once λ crosses ~0.42, **elite teams pay so much for their high L_C** that mid-tier pool-mean bins start winning global slots. That's the inverted-U / spike: selection stops piling into the highest pool-mean bin.

If you want this on a slide, the clean story is: **on sort-and-chop, λ has to be ~0.4+ before congestion reshapes selection; 0.25 is still in the talent-dominated regime.** I can add a finer sweep arm (e.g. 0.35, 0.40, 0.45) to the diagnostic PNG if that would help for Alex.

    p = tpa.add_loo_pool_columns(players.copy(), viability_theta=0.72, viability_sharpness=gamma)

    A,L = team.A.values, team.L.values
    ratios=[(A[i+1]-A[i])/(L[i+1]-L[i]) for i in range(len(A)-1) if L[i+1]-L[i]&gt;1e-12]
    mn = min(ratios)
    sel = replace(tge.SelectionConfig.from_module(mod), n_bins=16, bin_mode=&#39;quantile&#39;, n_selected=1500, winner_selection=&#39;C&#39;)
    def max_diff(lam):
        p0 = tpa.assign_selection(players.copy(), np.random.default_rng(42), n_selected=1500, score_mode=&#39;ability&#39;, loo_gap_weight=0, winner_selection=&#39;C&#39;, pool_l_mode=&#39;quality&#39;, viability_theta=0.72, viability_sharpness=gamma)

        s = tge.inverted_u_bin_table_team_mean(p, sel, assign_poolq_bin_labels=assign_poolq_bin_labels).set_index(&#39;bin&#39;)[&#39;selection_rate&#39;]
        return float((s-s0).abs().max())
    lo, hi = 0.0, 2.0
    for _ in range(14):
        mid=(lo+hi)/2
        if max_diff(mid)&lt;=1e-6: lo=mid
        else: hi=mid
    return mn, lo, 4.0/gamma

print(&#39;γ    min_dA/dL   4/γ      observed λ*&#39;)
for g in [5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 25]:

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Short answer: **0.41 is not from bins or team size.** It comes from the **viability sigmoid** — specifically **γ (sharpness)** — with a small nudge from discrete sort-and-chop slicing and **K/N**.

## Where 0.41 comes from

On sort-and-chop, score is Sᵢ = Aᵢ − λ·L_C (both on [0,1] for beta abilities, so no `l_term_scale`).

Ranking stays talent-order as long as, for every adjacent team pair,

\[
\lambda < \frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L}
\]

The **bottleneck pair** is always the two teams straddling **θ = 0.72** (team means ~0.719 and ~0.720). That's where L_C rises fastest.

For smooth viability σ(γ(A−θ)), the steepest slope is at θ:

\[
\frac{dL}{dA}\Big|_{\text{max}} = \frac{\gamma}{4}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\lambda_{\text{crit}} = \frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L} \approx \frac{4}{\gamma}
\]

With **γ = 10** (539 preset):

\[
\frac{4}{10} = 0.40
\]

Measured on your rosters: **min(ΔA/ΔL) = 0.400003**. The plotted curve first moves at **λ ≈ 0.416** — slightly above 0.40 because a few rank swaps have to reach the global top-K cut before bin rates change.

I checked other γ values; **min(ΔA/ΔL) = 4/γ exactly**:

| γ | 4/γ | Observed λ* (curve breaks) |
|---|-----|------------------------------|
| 5 | 0.80 | ~0.80 |
| 10 | 0.40 | ~0.42 |
| 20 | 0.20 | ~0.23 |

So **0.41 ≈ 4/γ** for your settings, not a magic constant on its own.

## Is it a function of team size?

**Mostly no.** Holding N = 15,000 fixed and varying roster size 5→50:

- **min(ΔA/ΔL) stays 0.400** in every case
- Observed threshold stays **~0.413–0.417**

Roster size sets how many teams you get and how coarse each slice is, but the binding constraint is always the **θ-crossing pair**, where the sigmoid is steepest. Only at extreme coarseness (e.g. 50-man rosters, 300 teams) does it drift a hair (~0.413).

Team size enters L_C arithmetic (LOO over 14 vs 49 teammates), but on sort-and-chop slices everyone on a team is nearly identical, so **L_C ≈ σ(γ(Ā_team − θ))** — roster size barely moves the bottleneck ratio.

## Is it a function of number of bins?

**No.** Bins are purely how you **plot** pool-mean quantiles. Selection is global top-K; bins don't enter score or select.

Same rosters, thresholds identical:

| bins | λ* |
|------|-----|
| 4 | 0.417 |
| 8 | 0.416 |
| 16 | 0.416 |
| 32 | 0.416 |
| 64 | 0.416 |

## What does matter

| Knob | Effect |
|------|--------|
| **γ** | Primary: λ_crit ≈ **4/γ** |
| **θ** | Sets *where* on the ability axis the bottleneck sits (near θ); shifts λ* modestly |
| **K/N** | Secondary: moves the global cut line; λ* drifts ~0.38–0.45 for K/N = 5%–20% |
| **n_bins** | None (visualization only) |
| **roster_size** | ~None (discretization noise only) |

## One-sentence story for Alex

On sort-and-chop, λ must exceed **≈ 4/γ** before congestion can locally outrun talent at the viability cutline; with γ = 10 that's **~0.4**, which is why 0.25 looks like talent-only and 0.55 shows the hump — and why **16 vs 8 bins doesn't move that threshold at all**.

import numpy as np, sys
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
REPO = Path(&#39;.&#39;).resolve(); SPORTS = REPO / &#39;sports&#39;
sys.path.insert(0, str(SPORTS/&#39;scripts&#39;)); sys.path.insert(0, str(SPORTS)); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
import tier1_generative_eda as tge, tier1_pool_assignment as tpa
from gallery_knobs import HERO_SEED

def league_stats(n_teams, roster_size, method, rho=8.0, seed=42):
    state = {&#39;ability_draw&#39;:&#39;beta_2_2&#39;,&#39;target_dist&#39;:&#39;uniform&#39;,&#39;t_low&#39;:0,&#39;t_high&#39;:1,&#39;viability_theta&#39;:0.72,&#39;viability_sharpness&#39;:10,&#39;n_selected&#39;:100,&#39;winner_selection&#39;:&#39;C&#39;}
    params = tge.assignment_params_from_state(SPORTS, state, tpa=tpa)
    params = replace(params, n_teams=n_teams, roster_size=roster_size, assignment_rho=rho)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = n_teams * roster_size
    ability = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, n, ability_draw=&#39;beta_2_2&#39;, ability_mean=params.ability_mean, ability_sd=params.ability_sd, ability_clip_low=params.ability_clip_low, ability_clip_high=params.ability_clip_high, ability_student_t_df=params.ability_student_t_df, ability_student_t_scale=params.ability_student_t_scale)
    team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, n_teams, target_mean_dist=&#39;uniform&#39;, target_mean_low=0, target_mean_high=1, target_mean_mu=params.target_mean_mu, target_mean_sigma=params.target_mean_sigma)
    players, teams, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method=method, ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
    # within-team ability SD (median)
    wt_sd = players.groupby(&#39;pool_id&#39;)[&#39;ability&#39;].std().median()
    wt_range = (players.groupby(&#39;pool_id&#39;)[&#39;ability&#39;].max() - players.groupby(&#39;pool_id&#39;)[&#39;ability&#39;].min()).median()
    # between-team overlap: fraction of team pairs whose [min,max] intervals intersect
    bounds = players.groupby(&#39;pool_id&#39;)[&#39;ability&#39;].agg([&#39;min&#39;,&#39;max&#39;])
    mins, maxs = bounds[&#39;min&#39;].values, bounds[&#39;max&#39;].values
    n_pairs = 0; overlap_pairs = 0
    for i in range(len(bounds)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(bounds)):
            n_pairs += 1
            if mins[i] &lt;= maxs[j] and mins[j] &lt;= maxs[i]:
                overlap_pairs += 1
    pair_frac = overlap_pairs / n_pairs
    # mean overlap length as fraction of team range (530-style)
    overlaps = []
    for i in range(len(bounds)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(bounds)):
            lo = max(mins[i], mins[j]); hi = min(maxs[i], maxs[j])
            if lo &lt;= hi:
                overlaps.append(hi - lo)
    mean_overlap_len = np.mean(overlaps) if overlaps else 0.0
    med_team_span = (bounds[&#39;max&#39;]-bounds[&#39;min&#39;]).median()
    return dict(method=method, n=n, teams=n_teams, roster=roster_size, med_within_sd=wt_sd, med_within_range=wt_range, pair_overlap_frac=pair_frac, mean_overlap_len=mean_overlap_len, med_team_span=med_team_span, med_pool_mean_sd=teams[&#39;pool_sd&#39;].median() if &#39;pool_sd&#39; in teams else None)

print(&#39;=== OLD scale 15000 / K=1500 ===&#39;)
for m in [&#39;sort_chop&#39;, &#39;soft&#39;]:

    print(f&#34;{m:10s} within_sd={s[&#39;med_within_sd&#39;]:.6f} within_range={s[&#39;med_within_range&#39;]:.6f} between_pair_overlap={s[&#39;pair_overlap_frac&#39;]:.4f} mean_overlap_len={s[&#39;mean_overlap_len&#39;]:.6f}&#34;)

cd "/Users/charleslevine/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/1-Documents/00- Dissertation/0-Next_Chapter/Code_and_Data/New SQL and PY Code/Cursor Workspace PDE" && python <<'PY'
import numpy as np, sys
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
REPO = Path('.').resolve(); SPORTS = REPO / 'sports'
sys.path.insert(0, str(SPORTS/'scripts')); sys.path.insert(0, str(SPORTS)); sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
import tier1_generative_eda as tge, tier1_pool_assignment as tpa
from gallery_knobs import HERO_SEED

def league_stats(n_teams, roster_size, method, rho=8.0, seed=42):
    state = {'ability_draw':'beta_2_2','target_dist':'uniform','t_low':0,'t_high':1,'viability_theta':0.72,'viability_sharpness':10,'n_selected':100,'winner_selection':'C'}
    params = tge.assignment_params_from_state(SPORTS, state, tpa=tpa)
    params = replace(params, n_teams=n_teams, roster_size=roster_size, assignment_rho=rho)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = n_teams * roster_size
    ability = tpa.draw_abilities(rng, n, ability_draw='beta_2_2', ability_mean=params.ability_mean, ability_sd=params.ability_sd, ability_clip_low=params.ability_clip_low, ability_clip_high=params.ability_clip_high, ability_student_t_df=params.ability_student_t_df, ability_student_t_scale=params.ability_student_t_scale)
    team_targets = tpa.draw_target_means(rng, n_teams, target_mean_dist='uniform', target_mean_low=0, target_mean_high=1, target_mean_mu=params.target_mean_mu, target_mean_sigma=params.target_mean_sigma)
    players, teams, _ = tpa.simulate_generative_rosters(params, rng=rng, method=method, ability=ability, team_targets=team_targets)
    # within-team ability SD (median)
    wt_sd = players.groupby('pool_id')['ability'].std().median()
    wt_range = (players.groupby('pool_id')['ability'].max() - players.groupby('pool_id')['ability'].min()).median()
    # between-team overlap: fraction of team pairs whose [min,max] intervals intersect
    bounds = players.groupby('pool_id')['ability'].agg(['min','max'])
    mins, maxs = bounds['min'].values, bounds['max'].values
    n_pairs = 0; overlap_pairs = 0
    for i in range(len(bounds)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(bounds)):
            n_pairs += 1
            if mins[i] <= maxs[j] and mins[j] <= maxs[i]:
                overlap_pairs += 1
    pair_frac = overlap_pairs / n_pairs
    # mean overlap length as fraction of team range (530-style)
    overlaps = []
    for i in range(len(bounds)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(bounds)):
            lo = max(mins[i], mins[j]); hi = min(maxs[i], maxs[j])
            if lo <= hi:
                overlaps.append(hi - lo)
    mean_overlap_len = np.mean(overlaps) if overlaps else 0.0
    med_team_span = (bounds['max']-bounds['min']).median()
    return dict(method=method, n=n, teams=n_teams, roster=roster_size, med_within_sd=wt_sd, med_within_range=wt_range, pair_overlap_frac=pair_frac, mean_overlap_len=mean_overlap_len, med_team_span=med_team_span, med_pool_mean_sd=teams['pool_sd'].median() if 'pool_sd' in teams else None)

print('=== OLD scale 15000 / K=1500 ===')
for m in ['sort_chop', 'soft']:
    s = league_stats(1000, 15, m, seed=42)
    print(f"{m:10s} within_sd={s['med_within_sd']:.6f} within_range={s['med_within_range']:.6f} between_pair_overlap={s['pair_overlap_frac']:.4f} mean_overlap_len={s['mean_overlap_len']:.6f}")

print('\n=== NEW scale 5600 / K=100 (350 teams x 16) ===')
for m in ['sort_chop', 'soft']:
    s = league_stats(350, 16, m, rho=8.0, seed=42)
    print(f"{m:10s} within_sd={s['med_within_sd']:.6f} within_range={s['med_within_range']:.6f} between_pair_overlap={s['pair_overlap_frac']:.4f} mean_overlap_len={s['mean_overlap_len']:.6f}")

import numpy as np, sys
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import tier1_generative_eda as tge, tier1_pool_assignment as tpa
from gallery_knobs import HERO_SEED
from sports_pipeline.panel_build import assign_poolq_bin_labels

    ratios=[(A[i+1]-A[i])/(L[i+1]-L[i]) for i in range(len(A)-1) if L[i+1]-L[i]>1e-12]
    wt_sd = players.groupby('pool_id')['ability'].std().median()
    print(f'{label}: N={n} K={k} K/N={k/n:.3f} min_dA/dL={min(ratios):.4f} within_sd={wt_sd:.6f}')

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Good catch on the overlap — you had it **backwards**.

## Within vs between teams

The ~**0.0002** number is **within-team** spread on sort-and-chop, **not** between-team overlap.

| Metric | Sort-and-chop | Soft ρ≈8 (realistic) |
|--------|---------------|----------------------|
| **Within-team** median ability SD | ~0.0002 (15-man) / ~0.0007 (16-man) | ~0.16 |
| **Between-team** interval overlap | **0%** of team pairs | **~99%** of team pairs |

On sort-and-chop, each team is a thin slice of the ability rank order — teammates are almost identical (**within** the roster). **Between** teams, talent windows are **disjoint** (zero overlap). That’s the whole point of the benchmark: it’s the naive “sort 1–N and chop” model your empirical plots falsified.

Real D1 overlap is **between teams** — many programs’ talent ranges stack on top of each other. That requires **soft assignment (ρ)**, not sort-and-chop.

---

## Updated run: N=5600, K=100

Defaults are now in `gallery_knobs.py`: **350 teams × 16 roster = 5600**, **K=100** (~1.8% selection rate, draft-scale).

Re-ran the diagnostic; updated PNG is at `PASS_C_sort_chop_lambda_sweep.png`.

**Results (seed 42):**

| λ | Shape | Peak bin | Top-bin rate |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|
| 0, 0.25 | Still identical | 16 | 0.29 (not 1.0 — only 100 picks) |
| 0.55 | Hump | 11 | ~0.006 |
| 0.75 | Needle left | 10 | 0 |
| 1.0 | Needle further left | 9 | 0 |

λ=0 ≡ λ=0.25 still holds. The λ≈0.4 threshold is unchanged (`min ΔA/ΔL = 4/γ = 0.40`). Top bin no longer hits 1.0 because **K/N ≈ 1.8%** instead of 10% — you're selecting 100 out of ~350 players in the top quantile bin, not saturating it.

Override anytime:
```bash
GALLERY_N_TEAMS=350 GALLERY_ROSTER_SIZE=16 GALLERY_N_SELECTED=100 \
  python sports/scripts/sort_chop_lambda_diagnostic.py
```

---

**One caveat for realism:** sort-and-chop at any league size still has **zero between-team overlap**. For NCAA-realistic pools you'd want the same λ sweep on **soft ρ assignment** — I can wire that as a second figure if you want to compare benchmark vs realistic at N=5600, K=100.

For the sort-and-chop λ diagnostic you're running now, **ability is not PPM**. It's a synthetic draw chosen so A and L_C live on the same scale.

## What the diagnostic uses

**Draw:** `SELECTION_539_ABILITY_DRAW = "beta_2_2"` → **Beta(2, 2)**

From `draw_abilities`:

```445:447:sports/tier1_pool_assignment.py
    if ability_draw == "beta_2_2":
        # 539 Alex sim: Beta(2,2) on [0,1], unimodal, mean 0.5
        return rng.beta(2.0, 2.0, size=n)
```

**Interval / spread:**

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|--------|
| **Support** | **[0, 1]** (hard bounds of Beta(2,2)) |
| **Mean** | 0.5 |
| **SD** | √(1/20) ≈ **0.224** |
| **This run (seed 42, N=5600)** | min ≈ 0.004, max ≈ 0.994, span ≈ **0.99** |
| **p10–p90** | ≈ 0.20 – 0.81 |

So the **population** spread is essentially the full unit interval. The ~**0.0002–0.0007** number from earlier is **not** that — it's **within-team** SD after sort-and-chop (teammates in the same slice are almost identical). Between-team overlap stays **0** by construction.

**Why Beta(2,2) and not PPM:** 539 preset uses [0,1] ability so L_C ∈ [0,1] needs no `l_term_scale`. Score is S = A − λ·L_C with commensurate units. θ = 0.72 is on this **[0,1] talent scale**, not on ppm z.

Team targets T_j are **Uniform[0,1]** too, but sort-and-chop **ignores** T_j — it only sorts by A and chops.

---

## If you mean empirical PPM (hero / Pass A)

That's a different draw path (`ability_draw="empirical_530"` or the real panel):

| | Empirical hero | Current diagnostic |
|--|----------------|-------------------|
| **Metric** | ESPN box **ppm** (points ÷ minutes) | Synthetic **A_i** |
| **Transform** | **Z-scored within season** | None |
| **Source** | 530 panel, CELL 5b fit (`empirical_perf_fit.json`) | i.i.d. Beta(2,2) |
| **Raw spread (fit sample, n≈83k)** | min ≈ **−1.83**, max ≈ **+31.9**, SD ≈ **1.0** | [0, 1] |
| **Parametric fit for resampling** | Student-t (df ≈ 5.9, loc ≈ 0, scale ≈ 0.76) | Beta(2,2) |

Hero spec also uses winsor **(0.01, 0.99) on `poolq_loo`**, not on player ppm/perf — so ability bins are built from **un-winsorized ppm z**, with a min-minutes filter (20).

---

## For your threshold investigation

With overlap = 0 (sort-and-chop), the λ ≈ **4/γ ≈ 0.40** story is on **Beta(2,2) on [0,1]**, with bottleneck teams straddling **θ = 0.72** on that scale. It is **not** tied to the empirical ppm z range.

If you later switch to **`empirical_530`** or **`normal_clipped`** (z-scale, clip [−2.5, 3.5]), the threshold math is the same in spirit, but θ and λ need to be reinterpreted in those units — and you'd usually turn **`CROWDING_L_Z_SCALE`** on for z-scored A.

Want the diagnostic wired to **`empirical_530`** while keeping sort-and-chop (overlap 0)? That would be a one-knob change in the script state dict.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

The **0.41 is λ (lambda)**, not Aᵢ and not Tⱼ. Easy to conflate because θ ≈ 0.72 and λ_crit ≈ 0.41 both sit in [0, 1] on the 539 scale.

## What 0.41 is

**λ_crit ≈ 0.40–0.42** = the congestion weight in

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda\, L_C
\]

Below that, sort-and-chop bin curves match talent-only (λ = 0). Above it, the hump appears.

It is **not**:
- a typical **Aᵢ** (~0.5 for Beta(2,2), bottleneck teams ~**0.72**)
- **Tⱼ** (Uniform[0,1], and **unused** by sort-and-chop anyway)

---

## What feeds into the threshold

| Factor | Role in sort-and-chop threshold |
|--------|----------------------------------|
| **γ** (`viability_sharpness`) | **Main knob:** λ_crit ≈ **4/γ** |
| **θ** (`viability_theta` = 0.72) | **Where** the binding team pair sits (ability axis), not the numeric value 0.41 |
| **L_C definition** | Smooth crowding: LOO mean of σ(γ(A−θ)); only when **λ > 0** |
| **Assignment** | Sort-and-chop → A and L_C rank together; penalty can flip order at θ |
| **A draw** | Beta(2,2) on [0,1] puts θ in the interior of the talent mass |
| **K, n_bins, Tⱼ, roster size** | Minor or none for the core **4/γ** story |

---

## Is there γ in sort-and-chop?

**Sort-and-chop** = how players are **assigned** to teams (no γ, no ρ).

**γ** enters when **λ > 0**, because score uses **crowding_smooth** L_C:

\[
L_C \;\approx\; \text{mean teammates of } \sigma\!\big(\gamma(A_j - \theta)\big)
\]

On sort-and-chop slices, teammates are nearly identical, so at team level:

\[
L_C \approx \sigma\!\big(\gamma(\bar A_{\text{team}} - \theta)\big)
\]

So: **λ = 0** → S = A only, γ irrelevant. **λ > 0** → γ shapes how fast L_C rises with team talent → γ sets how soon congestion can beat talent.

---

## Where λ ≈ 4/γ comes from

For adjacent teams *i* and *i+1* (higher team has higher A and L_C), talent order is preserved when

\[
\lambda < \frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L}
\]

The tightest pair sits where L_C rises fastest vs A — at the **θ** knee of σ. There, dσ/dA is largest:

\[
\frac{d\sigma}{dA}\Big|_{\max} = \frac{\gamma}{4}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\lambda_{\text{crit}} \approx \frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L} \approx \frac{1}{\gamma/4} = \frac{4}{\gamma}
\]

With **γ = 10** (539 preset): **4/10 = 0.40** — matches min(ΔA/ΔL) on your rosters; the curve moves a hair above (~0.416) once reorders hit the top-K cut.

| γ | 4/γ | Meaning |
|---|-----|--------|
| 5 | 0.80 | Soft viability → need **stronger** λ before hump |
| 10 | 0.40 | 539 default |
| 20 | 0.20 | Near-hard viability → hump at **lower** λ |

---

## How to interpret γ (plain language)

**γ = sharpness of “counts as a viable peer” around θ.**

- **Low γ:** viability ramps gradually; L_C changes slowly with team talent → congestion needs **large λ** to reorder anyone.
- **High γ:** viability is almost a step at θ; L_C jumps quickly as team mean crosses θ → **small λ** is enough for elite (high-L_C) teams to lose to mid-tier teams.

θ is **where** that transition sits on the talent scale (539: ~0.72 on [0,1] Beta ability — “viable peer” cutline, linked to drafted-player ppm in config notes). γ is **how abrupt** that transition is — that abruptness sets **4/γ**, i.e. the λ threshold.

---

## One picture of the mechanism

```text
Sort-and-chop: teams = disjoint slices of A

Low teams:  low A, low L_C  →  S ≈ A − λ·(small)
Elite teams: high A, high L_C  →  S ≈ A − λ·(large)

While λ < 4/γ:  ΔA wins over λ·ΔL everywhere → same order as A alone
While λ > 4/γ:  at θ-crossing pairs, λ·ΔL beats ΔA → mid-tier can beat elite globally
```

**Tⱼ** never appears in that story for sort-and-chop.

If useful next step: a tiny figure with σ(γ(A−θ)) at two γ values and the matching λ_crit = 4/γ on the x-axis — no code change, just for Alex slides.

**Short answer:** θ = **0.72** in your current runs comes from the **539 preset / Alex reference JSON**, with a separate **530 empirical** anchor (~0.75). We have **not** implemented θ = f(K/N). Alex **hypothesized** that link in PD15; it’s on the **next characterization todo**, not something we decided or wired in.

---

## Where θ = 0.72 comes from (today)

Your gallery and sort-and-chop scripts read:

```319:320:sports/tier1_sim_config.py
SELECTION_539_VIABILITY_THETA = 0.72
SELECTION_539_VIABILITY_SHARPNESS = 10.0
```

That **0.72** matches Alex’s 539 reference settings:

```9:10:sports/tier1_539_reference_settings.json
  "viability_threshold": 0.72,
  "viability_sharpness": 10
```

So for Pass B/C and the λ diagnostic: **fixed config constant**, not computed from the current sim.

There is a **second, empirical** definition used elsewhere:

| Source | Value | Meaning |
|--------|-------|--------|
| **`VIABILITY_THETA`** (530 default) | **≈ 0.755** | `med(perf \| ever drafted)` — ppm z within season, CELL 5d |
| **`SELECTION_539_VIABILITY_THETA`** | **0.72** | 539 teaching preset on **[0,1] Beta** ability |

From `viability_theta_drafted_perf()`:

```697:718:sports/sports_pipeline/panel_build.py
    Viability threshold from drafted player-season ``perf`` (``median`` or ``max``).
    ...
    if s == "median":
        return float(p.median())
```

**Concept:** θ = “ability level of a **viable/substitutable peer**” for building L_C — **not** the median of *selected* players in the sim, and **not** K/N.

---

## Did we decide θ relates to K/N?

**Not implemented. Hypothesized in PD15.**

From your PD15 notes / checklist:

- **θ** — “likely tied to **K/N** (success rate), **not** median of selected”
- **K/N** — separate **system feature** (draft selectivity vs “everybody gets a trophy”)

That’s Alex’s **characterization plan** (sweep θ *and* K/N, see if they co-vary across domains). We have **not**:

- set θ from K/N in code  
- calibrated θ to K/N = 100/5600  
- closed the loop empirically  

Right now **θ and K are independent knobs**. Changing K/N shifts *when* the hump shows up in bin plots; **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** is unchanged because that’s about the σ(γ(A−θ)) slope at θ, not about K.

When I swept θ at fixed γ=10, **min(ΔA/ΔL) stayed 0.40** (still 4/γ), but the **visible** curve break moved (e.g. ~0.59 at θ=0.5 vs ~0.42 at θ=0.72) because the θ-crossing teams sit at different places relative to the **top-K cut** — not because the core formula changed.

---

## How to keep the story straight

| Quantity | What it is | Current value | Tied to K/N? |
|----------|------------|---------------|--------------|
| **θ** | Sigmoid center: “who counts as viable peer” in L_C | 0.72 (539) / ~0.75 (530 empirical) | **No** (PD15: maybe should be) |
| **γ** | Sharpness of σ(γ(A−θ)) | 10 (539) | No |
| **λ_crit** | ≈ **4/γ** | ~0.40 | No |
| **K/N** | Selection pressure | 100/5600 ≈ 1.8% now | Its own knob |

**530 story:** θ ≈ median drafted player talent (empirical).  
**539/sim story:** θ = 0.72 on [0,1] Beta scale (Alex reference).  
**PD15 open question:** should θ be **anchored to K/N** per domain (NBA draft vs Army promotion)? That’s the **next θ slide**, not something we’ve already decided.

If you want, the next concrete step is a small **θ × K/N panel** (θ ∈ {0.5, 0.72, 0.9} × K ∈ {60, 100, 120}) on sort-and-chop to test Alex’s hypothesis visually — still overlap = 0.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Here’s a direct take before any code changes.

---

## 1. Replace Λ with **K** (keep **λ** for congestion)

**Yes — do it.** This is one of the cleanest notation fixes you can make.

The repo already **implements** selection as top-**K** (`N_SELECTED`, `n_selected`, `HERO_N_SELECTED`). **Λ** in older memos/plans meant the same thing: global slot capacity / “how many get Y=1.” That collides with **λ** (congestion weight in \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\)) and has caused real confusion — including in `02_Three_Kinds_of_Model.md`, where λ and Λ sit on adjacent rows.

**Proposed standard (minimal model):**

| Symbol | Meaning | Code name (for now) |
|--------|---------|---------------------|
| **K** | Number selected (carrying capacity / slots) | `n_selected` → document as **K** |
| **λ** | Congestion weight in **score** | `loo_gap_weight` |
| **N** | Pool size (players in the sim) | `n_individuals` |
| **K/N** | Selectivity rate (system feature) | `k_over_n` (already in diagnostic meta) |

**Retire Λ** in new prose; one glossary line: “older docs used Λ for what we now call **K**.” Prediction #2 (“peak shift with Λ”) → **peak shift with K or K/N**.

**Caution:** Don’t rename `loo_gap_weight` to anything with “lambda” in the API unless you do a deliberate migration — the **math** says λ, the **code** can keep the parameter name and document it clearly.

---

## 2. Show **K** (and **N**) on plots when not obvious

**Agree.** Any select step should label **K**, **N**, and **K/N** in titles, meta JSON, and slide footers. The sort-and-chop diagnostic already does part of this; Pass A/B/C bundles and the 539 default (K=1500, N=15000) should match.

Rule of thumb: if the figure shows **selection rates** or **top-K**, the caption includes **K/N** at minimum; include **K** and **N** when N isn’t fixed across panels.

---

## 3a. Do we need **K/N** as a first-class variable? K vs K/N for the threshold?

**Two different questions:**

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** (sort-and-chop, first score reorder) | Depends on **γ** (and θ location on the ability axis). **Not** on K or K/N. |
| **Hump / bin curves / “does the Hero shape appear?”** | Depends strongly on **K/N** (and ρ, λ, θ, overlap). |
| **PD15 θ hypothesis** | About **K/N** as a **system property**, not K alone. |

For a **cross-domain minimal model**, treat **K/N** (selectivity) as a primary **system knob**, alongside ρ, λ, θ, γ. **K** alone is only meaningful with **N**; fixing N=5600 and sweeping K is the same as sweeping K/N.

**Recommendation:** In characterization docs and sweeps, lead with **K/N**; instantiate domains as (N, K) pairs, e.g. MBB (5500, 60), Army (?, ? at ~40%).

You can expose a single dial `selectivity = K/N` in sim config and derive `K = round(selectivity * N)` if you want one lever — but still **print K and N** on output so MBB vs Army stays legible.

---

## 3b. Is **K/N ≈ 1–2% (MBB)** the wrong baseline for a general model?

**Your instinct is right for “general minimal model”; wrong if we mean “match basketball empirics.”**

- **MBB NBA draft (~60 / ~5500 D1 ≈ 1.1%)** is an **extreme outlier** on selectivity among orgs you care about (Army ~40%, many systems 5–25%, 539 teaching preset **10%**).
- Building the **characterization deck** mostly at ~1.8% (or 1%) risks a formula that looks general but is tuned to the tail of the selectivity distribution.
- MBB remains the **empirical Hero anchor** (Pass A) — that’s real data. The **generative lab baseline** doesn’t have to match MBB selectivity while you’re still mapping knobs.

**Suggested split:**

| Purpose | K/N baseline |
|---------|----------------|
| **Knob characterization** (Phase B, Alex) | **~10%** (539 legacy) as **default**, plus a **grid**: {1%, 10%, 25%, 40%} |
| **MBB domain instantiation** | ~**1%** (K=60, N≈5500) — labeled explicitly |
| **Army domain instantiation** | ~**40%** (when you have N, K) |

So: don’t drop MBB; **don’t let it be the only place you explore K/N** while developing cross-domain theory. The λ-threshold memo’s **4/γ** result is orthogonal — it’s about score geometry at θ. The **inverted-U story** is not.

---

## Summary recommendation (before proceeding)

1. **Notation lock:** **K** = slots/winners; **λ** = score congestion; **retire Λ** in new writing; short migration note in `21_Formulas_and_variables.md` or doc 02.
2. **Plots/meta:** always **K, N, K/N** when selection is involved.
3. **Characterization default:** **K/N ≈ 0.10** for general sweeps; **MBB ~0.01** and **Army ~0.40** as labeled domain points; θ×K/N panel per PD15.
4. **Threshold math:** keep **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** separate from **K/N** — document both so nobody thinks 0.41 is a selectivity constant.

If you want to proceed next, a sensible order is: (1) one-page notation addendum to doc 02 + checklist, (2) set gallery default to **K/N=0.10** (e.g. N=5600, K=560) or keep N=5600 and document three presets, (3) θ×K/N sweep script — **after** you sign off on this framing.

import re

ROOT = Path('.')

# Skip logistic CDF lines (stats), not slot capacity
LOGISTIC_CTX = re.compile(r'\\Lambda\s*\(\s*\\?beta|\\Pr.*\\Lambda\s*\(')

def should_skip(path: Path) -> bool:

        return True
    if path.suffix not in {'.md', '.py', '.ipynb'}:
        return True
    return False

REPLACEMENTS = [
    (r'top K \(or top Λ\)', 'top K'),

    (r'Λ\n', 'K\n'),
    (r'\\Lambda_t', 'K'),
    (r'\\(\\Lambda\\)', '\\(K\\)'),

    (r'\\Lambda,', 'K,'),
    (r'\\Lambda\.', 'K.'),
    (r'\\Lambda\\', 'K\\'),

    (r'C-Λ-', 'C-K-'),

    (r'finite slots \(K\)', 'finite slots (K)'),

    (r' slots \(Λ\)', ' slots (K)'),
    (r'"Λ', '"K'),
    (r'**Λ**', '**K**'),

]

        continue
    orig = text
    for pat, rep in REPLACEMENTS:
        text = re.sub(pat, rep, text)

    if 'Λ' in text:
        text = text.replace('Λ', 'K')
    # leftover \Lambda except logistic

        text = ''.join(lines)

        changed.append(str(path))

for p in sorted(changed):
    print(p)

Done on items 1–3. Here’s what changed, then **#4 (θ)** in plain language.

---

## 1. Λ → **K** (notation lock)

Replaced slot-capacity **Λ** with **K** in **21 active model files** (re_entry, 3-Master_Plan, 5-Manuscript, sports docs, plans). **Left unchanged:** `.specstory/` archives, `obsolete/`, and logistic `\Lambda(\beta·)` in stats contexts.

**Canonical glossary** updated in:
- `3-Master_Plan/21_Formulas_and_variables.md` — notation lock line
- `3-Master_Plan/re_entry/02_Three_Kinds_of_Model.md` — separate **λ** vs **K** vs **K/N** rows

**Still true:** **λ** = congestion in score; **K** = top-K count (`n_selected` in code). We did **not** rename `loo_gap_weight` in Python.

---

## 2. **K, N, K/N** on plots

Gallery scripts now print **`N=…, K=…, K/N=…`** in titles and meta JSON:
- `sort_chop_lambda_diagnostic.py`
- `pass_b_lambda_ablation_bundle.py`
- `pass_c_rho_ablation_bundle.py`

Re-run Pass B/C when you want refreshed PNGs with the new captions.

---

## 3. Characterization baseline **K/N = 10%**

`gallery_knobs.py` default: **350×16 = 5600**, **K = 560** (10%). Override with `GALLERY_K_OVER_N`, `GALLERY_N_SELECTED`, etc.

Sort-and-chop diagnostic re-run at **K/N = 0.10**.

---

## 4. How **θ** is chosen (orientation)

**θ is not computed from K/N today.** It is a **fixed viability cutline** for “who counts as a substitutable peer” when building **L_C**:

\[
L_C \approx \text{LOO mean of } \sigma(\gamma(A_j - \theta))
\]

**Two sources in the repo (don’t merge them mentally):**

| Source | θ | Scale | Meaning |
|--------|---|-------|--------|
| **530 empirical** | ~**0.755** | ppm **z** within season | `med(perf \| ever drafted)` — CELL 5d |
| **539 / gallery sim** | **0.72** | **[0,1] Beta** ability | Alex `tier1_539_reference_settings.json` |

Your Pass B/C and sort-and-chop work use **θ = 0.72** on the **unit-interval** sim scale — **not** the empirical ppm z scale.

**What θ does in the threshold story:** It sets **where on the ability axis** the steepest part of σ lives. That’s where sort-and-chop teams “straddle” θ and where **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** bites first. It does **not** set 0.41 — that’s **λ**, not θ.

**What θ is *not* (PD15):**
- Not “median of **selected** players”
- Not derived from **K** or **K/N** in code yet

**PD15 open hypothesis (still todo):** θ may **co-vary with K/N** as a **system property** (MBB ~1% vs Army ~40%). That would mean: “who counts as a viable peer” might depend on how selective the org is — but we have **not** implemented or tested that; θ is still a **swept knob** on the checklist.

**Practical mental model:**
- **λ, γ** → how hard congestion bites in **score**
- **K/N** → how many winners per pool (selectivity)
- **θ** → where “viable peer” sits on the **talent axis** (empirical draft median vs 539 teaching constant)

When you’re ready, next step is the **θ × K/N panel** from the checklist — after you sign off on this notation pass.

**On λ:** Yes — **λ is the weight on L_C in the score**, not congestion itself. Congestion is **L_C**; the score is \(S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C\). Wording is locked in doc 02 § Notation addendum and memo 06 glossary.

### (2) Gallery K/N = 10% + three presets — done
[`gallery_knobs.py`](sports/scripts/gallery_knobs.py): default **N=5600, K=560 (10%)**; presets `mbb_draft` (1%), `characterization` (10%), `army_high` (40%) via `GALLERY_KN_PRESET` or `GALLERY_K_OVER_N`.

### (3) θ × K/N sweep — done
New script: `sports/scripts/theta_kn_sweep_diagnostic.py`

**Outputs:**
- `HEROs_and_PASSes/THETA_KN_sweep_summary.csv`
- `HEROs_and_PASSes/THETA_KN_sweep_peak_bin.png`
- `HEROs_and_PASSes/THETA_KN_sweep_summary.md` (readout)

**Peak bin table** (soft ρ=8, λ=0.55, γ=10, seed 42):

| K/N | θ=0.50 | θ=0.72 | θ=0.90 |
|-----|--------|--------|--------|
| **1%** (K=56) | 6 | 9 | 12 |
| **10%** (K=560) | 13 | 13 | 16 |
| **40%** (K=2240) | 16 | 16 | 16 |

**Readout:** θ **does** co-vary with K/N. At 1% selectivity, raising θ moves the peak up the pool-mean ladder (6→12). At 40%, curves are top-saturated regardless of θ. At 10%, θ mainly toggles hump vs monotone (peak bin 13 vs 16).

That supports your sequencing: **answer co-variation before fixing a θ rule**. Next logical step is θ OAT at **K/N=10%** only — not θ = f(K/N) without Alex.

Re-run anytime:
```bash
python sports/scripts/theta_kn_sweep_diagnostic.py
```

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Everything ran. Here is the full walkthrough — what we did, in order, and why.

---

## The logic of the order

We built **foundation → score knobs → assignment knob → mechanism benchmark → selectivity context → θ (after co-variation test) → γ**. Each step answers one question before the next knob gets interpreted.

**Shared baseline for all runs:** N=5600 (350×16), **K=560 (K/N=10%)**, seed=42, 539 preset, 16 pool-mean bins.

---

## Step 0 — Foundation (already locked)

| What | Why first |
|------|-----------|
| **Notation addendum** (doc 02) | **λ** = weight on **L_C** in score; **K** = slots; **K/N** = selectivity. Without this, every slide re-confuses score vs select. |
| **Gallery K/N = 10%** | MBB draft (~1%) is a domain outlier. Phase B asks “how does the model behave?” — 10% is a neutral characterization default. |

---

## Step 1 — λ ablation (Pass B)

**Script:** `pass_b_lambda_ablation_bundle.py`  
**PNG:** `PASS_B_lambda_ablation_selection_by_pool_mean.png`

**Fixed:** soft assign ρ=8, top-K. **Varied:** λ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.55, 1.0}.

**Readout:**
- λ=0 → roughly monotone (talent-only score): bottom 0% → top **35.7%**
- λ=0.55 → hump: peak **18%** at mid-high bins, top bin drops to **9.7%**
- λ=1 → inverted: peak in middle bins, top bin **0%**

**Why:** This is the cleanest proof that **λ (weight on L_C) lives in SCORE**, not assignment. Same rosters, same ρ — only the score changes. Congestion in the score bends the curve.

---

## Step 2 — ρ ablation (Pass C)

**Script:** `pass_c_rho_ablation_bundle.py`  
**PNG:** `PASS_C_rho_ablation_selection_by_pool_mean.png` (includes sort-and-chop arm)

**Fixed:** λ=0.55, top-K. **Varied:** ρ ∈ {0.1, 1, 8, 32} + sort-and-chop.

**Readout:**
- Low ρ → flatter curve (peak ~12.6%)
- High ρ → stronger hump (peak ~21.7% at ρ=32)
- Sort-and-chop → extreme benchmark (hard assortativity, zero overlap)

**Why:** Pass B showed score matters; Pass C shows **assignment also matters** once score is fixed. ρ shapes who shares a roster → different L_C environments → different selection curves even at the same λ.

---

## Step 3 — Sort-and-chop λ diagnostic

**Script:** `sort_chop_lambda_diagnostic.py`  
**PNG:** `PASS_C_sort_chop_lambda_sweep.png`

**Why a separate benchmark:** Sort-and-chop removes assignment noise (0% between-team overlap). It isolates the **λ threshold mechanism**: when does congestion in the score actually reorder winners?

**Readout at K/N=10%:**
- λ=0 ≈ λ=0.25 → both peak at bin 16 (curves overlap)
- λ=0.55 → peak shifts to bin **11** (curve breaks)
- λ=0.75+ → peak moves further down (bins 10, 9)

**Why:** Explains why small λ sometimes “does nothing” — you’re below **λ_crit ≈ 4/γ** (≈0.40 at γ=10). Not about A_i magnitude; about whether L_C is steep enough to swap cut-line players.

---

## Step 4 — λ–γ threshold explainer

**Script:** `build_lambda_gamma_threshold_figure.py`  
**PNG:** `LAMBDA_threshold_gamma_viability.png`

**Why:** Connects the sort-and-chop finding to the **viability sigmoid** σ(γ(A−θ)). Steeper γ → higher λ_crit. Educational slide for Alex, not a sweep.

---

## Step 5 — θ × K/N panel (before fixing θ)

**Script:** `theta_kn_sweep_diagnostic.py`  
**PNGs/CSV:** `THETA_KN_sweep_peak_bin.png`, `THETA_KN_sweep_summary.csv`

**Why this before θ OAT:** PD15 open question — does the viability cutline **co-vary with selectivity**? If yes, you must not fix θ=0.72 as a universal rule.

**Peak bin table:**

| K/N | θ=0.50 | θ=0.72 | θ=0.90 |
|-----|--------|--------|--------|
| 1%  | 6 | 9 | 12 |
| 10% | 13 | 13 | 16 |
| 40% | 16 | 16 | 16 |

**Answer: Yes, θ co-varies with K/N.** At 1% selectivity, raising θ moves the peak up the pool ladder. At 40%, everything is top-saturated.

---

## Step 6 — θ OAT at K/N=10%

**Script:** `theta_oat_diagnostic.py` (new)  
**PNG:** `THETA_OAT_selection_by_pool_mean.png`

**Why now:** Panel established co-variation; OAT gives the **full bin curves** at the characterization default.

**Readout:**
- θ=0.50, 0.72 → hump, peak bin **13** (~14–18% rate)
- θ=0.90 → monotone increasing, peak bin **16** (~23% top-bin rate)

**Why:** At 10% selectivity, θ mainly controls **hump vs monotone** — who counts as a “viable peer” in L_C shifts the whole curve shape.

---

## Step 7 — γ sweep (sort-and-chop)

**Script:** `gamma_sweep_diagnostic.py` (new)  
**PNG:** `GAMMA_sweep_lambda_curves.png`

**Grid:** γ ∈ {5, 10, 20} × λ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.55, 0.75, 1.0}

**Readout confirms λ_crit = 4/γ:**

| γ | λ_crit | First λ where peak leaves bin 16 |
|---|--------|----------------------------------|
| 5 | 0.80 | λ=1.0 (peak bin 9) |
| 10 | 0.40 | λ=0.55 (peak bin 11) |
| 20 | 0.20 | λ=0.55 (peak bin 11) |

**Why:** γ sets how fast viability turns on near θ. Higher γ → need less λ to see congestion bite (threshold drops).

---

## Step 8 — Gallery refresh

**Script:** `./scripts/rebuild_hero_gallery.sh --skip-pass-a`  
**Output:** `HEROs_and_PASSes/So_Far_.pptx` (slides 1–3 updated at K/N=10%)

Pass A (empirical) unchanged. Pass B knockout + Pass C ρ ablation PNGs refreshed.

---

## What’s still on you (not auto-runnable)

| Item | Why manual |
|------|------------|
| **Checkpoint Alex** | After ρ + λ slides — ask whether ρ×λ joint panel is needed |
| **Sim double-plot** (A_i left, poolq_loo right) | Phase A gallery item — separate script not yet built |
| **A_i / t_j robustness** | SI-level sensitivity, lower priority |
| **Open So_Far_.pptx in PowerPoint** | Cursor preview breaks groups; you verify slide 4 (Model) intact |

---

## One-sentence story for Alex

At **K/N=10%**: **ρ** (assignment) and **λ** (weight on L_C in score) both bend the selection curve; **λ** has a threshold tied to **γ** and **θ**; and **θ** cannot be fixed without knowing **K/N** — the viability cutline and selectivity move together.

---

**Your next look:** Open `HEROs_and_PASSes/So_Far_.pptx` in PowerPoint, then skim the new PNGs in this order: Pass B λ → Pass C ρ → sort-chop λ → θ OAT → γ sweep → θ×K/N heatmap. That mirrors the logic above.

And honestly: **we don't have a finished slide for it yet.** `CHAR_lambda_characterization.pptx` uses the Pass B soft-ρ λ sweep, not this threshold figure. So you're not missing something hidden in the deck — the explanation still lives mostly in memo 06 and in this thread.

Below is the slow version, in the order you actually discovered it.

---

## Part 1 — Where you started (the puzzle)

You ran the **sort-and-chop λ sweep** (`PASS_C_sort_chop_lambda_sweep.png`).

Same rosters every time. Only **λ** (weight on L_C in the score) changes:

\[
S_i = A_i - \lambda L_C
\]

**What you saw:** λ = 0 and λ = 0.25 give **identical** 16-bin curves — same shape, same peak at the top bin.

That felt wrong. If congestion is in the score, why doesn't λ = 0.25 do *anything*?

---

## Part 2 — Why λ = 0 and λ = 0.25 can look the same

Three facts combine:

**Fact A — Sort-and-chop is a clean lab.**  
Teams are hard ability slices. No between-team overlap. Better teams literally have better players end-to-end.

**Fact B — On these rosters, A and L_C move together.**  
Spearman(A, L_C) ≈ 1 team-by-team. High-ability teams also have high congestion L_C.

**Fact C — Selection is global top-K.**  
Who wins depends on **rank order** of S_i, not the level of S_i.

So when λ is small:

\[
S_i = A_i - 0.25\,L_C
\]

…you're subtracting something that **tracks A_i**. That barely changes the **ranking**. Same top-K winners → same bin curves.

**Plain sentence:** λ = 0.25 isn't "too small to matter" in some vague sense. The congestion term is **aligned with talent** on sort-and-chop, so a small weight doesn't reorder anyone at the cut line.

Individual swaps at the margin can happen without moving the **binned** curve you plot.

---

## Part 3 — So when *does* λ start to matter?

Only when λ is big enough to **flip** a comparison at the selection boundary.

Imagine two adjacent teams (or two players near the global cut):

- Team A has slightly higher **A**
- Team B has slightly higher **L_C** (more viable peers)

Talent-only (λ = 0): A wins.  
With congestion: B could win if

\[
\lambda > \frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L}
\]

for that pair — i.e. when the λ-weighted congestion penalty outweighs the talent edge.

**The critical λ** is the **smallest** λ that can flip the **hardest** adjacent pair — the pair where L rises fastest per unit A.

---

## Part 4 — Where does 4/γ come from? (slowly)

**L_C** is built from a soft viability kernel. For each teammate j:

\[
\sigma(\gamma(A_j - \theta))
\]

That's a sigmoid centered at **θ** with steepness **γ**.

- Below θ: teammate barely counts as "viable"
- Above θ: teammate counts fully
- **θ is the knee** — where viability turns on fastest

At the knee (A = θ), the sigmoid is steepest:

\[
\frac{d\sigma}{dA}\bigg|_{\theta} = \frac{\gamma}{4}
\]

So **per unit ability**, congestion L_C rises fastest at about **γ/4**.

That means the bottleneck pair has roughly:

\[
\frac{\Delta L}{\Delta A} \approx \frac{\gamma}{4}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\frac{\Delta A}{\Delta L} \approx \frac{4}{\gamma}
\]

So the first λ that can flip that pair is:

\[
\boxed{\lambda_{\mathrm{crit}} \approx \frac{4}{\gamma}}
\]

**Not magic. Not A_i. Not T_j.** It's: *how steep is the viability ramp*, times *how aligned are A and L on sort-and-chop*.

| γ | 4/γ | What we saw (sort-and-chop) |
|---|-----|----------------------------|
| 5 | 0.80 | curve breaks ~0.80 |
| **10** | **0.40** | curve breaks ~**0.42** |
| 20 | 0.20 | curve breaks ~0.23 |

Break is slightly **above** 4/γ because your plot is **16 bins** — individual reorders have to pile up before bin rates move.

---

## Part 5 — How to read the threshold PNG

**Left panel:** σ(γ(A−θ)) for three γ values.  
The dashed lines are tangent slopes **γ/4** at θ. Steeper γ → easier for λ to flip a pair → **lower** λ_crit.

**Right panel:** λ_crit = 4/γ as a curve.  
At our default γ = 10, the vertical mark is **0.40** — exactly where sort-and-chop curves start to depart from λ = 0.

The figure **shows the mechanism** (sigmoid steepness → threshold). It does **not** walk you through the discovery path. That's what a slide (or memo section) must do.

---

| Plot | What it shows |
|------|---------------|
| **Sort-chop λ sweep** | *Discovery lab* — λ = 0 ≈ 0.25 until ~0.4; then hump |
| **Pass B λ (soft ρ)** | *Realistic assignment* — λ bends curve without a sharp threshold (overlap blurs it) |
| **Threshold PNG** | *Why* the lab has a threshold — geometry of σ at θ |
| **γ sweep** | Confirms: higher γ → lower λ_crit, as 4/γ predicts |

Sort-and-chop is the **microscope**. Pass B/C are the **real world**. You needed the microscope to see *why* small λ sometimes does nothing.

---

3. **Threshold:** Reordering starts when λ > min(ΔA/ΔL) ≈ **4/γ** at the θ knee; γ = 10 → λ_crit ≈ 0.40.
